messages:
Samira (support): heads up — customer (acme-ads) reporting intermittent 401s from CI when uploading artifacts to the Redwood API. started ~after we tightened rwd-ci-bot sessionDuration to 1h. failures only on long jobs (~1.5h).

Jorge (eng): logs or a sample error payload? that sounds like token expiry mid-job or audience mismatch.

Samira (support): paste from their runner logs: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2026 09:22:11 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "error_description": "Token has expired or audience mismatch: aud=gitlab-job-1234"
}
```

Maya (security): aud showing job id is interesting — do they use an OIDC flow that sets aud to the job? or is the impersonation helper doing that?

gitlab-runner-bot: The customer recently switched to workload-identity-proxy v2 for short-lived OIDC tokens. by default it sets aud to the job id for replay protection.

Jorge (eng): ok — two things to check: 1) are they actually impersonating rwd-ci-bot or exchanging OIDC token directly? 2) where did the token minting occur relative to the long-running job steps (i.e., is token minted at pipeline start and never refreshed)?

Samira (support): they were previously using `gcloud --impersonate-service-account` in a helper step (minting a token per-step). after migrating to the proxy, the proxy caches tokens per-run and the upload step can be >1h after mint time. reproducible locally with impersonation too:

```
# repro (local):
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=rwd-ci-bot@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/upload -d @artifact.tar
# => 401 invalid_token (aud=gitlab-job-1234)
```

Maya (security): two separate problems likely: (A) audience mismatch — our API expects tokens with aud=https://api.redwood.inference (or cloud-platform) and rejects job-scoped aud; (B) sessionDuration/ttl — if the token lifetime is shorter than the job step gap, you'll see expiry mid-job. we tightened sessionDuration to 1h which affects impersonated tokens if the impersonation flow honours that.

Jorge (eng): short-term mitigation: instruct the runner/proxy to request a new token immediately before the upload step (refresh). long-term: either accept additional aud values for impersonation tokens (less preferred) or add an explicit token-exchange endpoint for CI that issues API-scoped tokens via an internal exchange.

Samira (support): shared quick mitigation script with customer and they confirmed it fixed the upload step. script below they added as a pre-upload job step: 

```
# refresh-token.sh (pre-upload)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=rwd-ci-bot@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
export ACCESS_TOKEN
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/upload -d @artifact.tar
```

gitlab-runner-bot: alt: configure workload-identity-proxy with `audience: https://api.redwood.inference` or enable per-step token refresh in the proxy (see proxy docs).

Maya (security): follow-ups:
- update our CI integration docs to call out aud mismatch with job-scoped OIDC tokens and recommended configs
- consider adding a small server-side compatibility layer that accepts our impersonation aud or performs a token exchange for CI flows
- ops: monitor for increased 401 rates tied to rwd-ci-bot and alert if >5% of uploads fail with invalid_token

Jorge (eng): I'll file an internal ticket to evaluate token-exchange endpoint and add a console check to detect stale tokens in diagnostics.

Samira (support): customer applied the pre-upload refresh and confirms green. closing the immediate escalation. adding docs task and infra ticket. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment note — no rollout required. added link to customer thread in the support ticket.
